description: GitHub repository exists with a clean baseline commit containing the repo skeleton, AGENTS.md, logs, wiki index and research captures.
steps: Run `gh auth status` — it reports being logged in to a GitHub host
Run `git -C '<repo>' log --oneline -1` and confirm a commit exists with message 'chore: project baseline'
Run `git -C '<repo>' status --porcelain` — it outputs nothing
Open the repository on github.com and confirm README.md is visible in the file listing

description: Repository README exists in both English and Russian, describing the project, the north star, the stack and the current phase.
steps: Open README.md — it is written in English and links to the Russian version
Open README.ru.md — it is written in Russian and links back to the English version
Both files state the north star ('first real commission received') and list the confirmed stack (TypeScript, Node 22, Next.js static-first, Cloudflare, SQLite dev / Postgres prod)
Both files link to docs/roadmap/ROADMAP.md and docs/wiki/INDEX.md

description: LLM-wiki INDEX.md lists every wiki page in the docs/wiki tree, and every page listed actually exists.
steps: Run: Get-ChildItem docs/wiki -Recurse -Filter *.md | ForEach-Object { $_.FullName } — collect the paths
Run a grep for every wiki link in docs/wiki/INDEX.md and confirm each resolves to a file on disk
Confirm there are zero wiki .md files on disk that are absent from INDEX.md
Confirm every page that is still pending research is marked with a confidence value or an explicit pending marker

description: Subagent definitions exist under .opencode/agents/ for explorer, researcher, architect, implementer, verifier and analyst, and each inherits the no-deletion rule.
steps: List .opencode/agents/ — six agent definition files are present
Open each file and confirm it contains the R1 no-deletion rule and the never-fabricate rule
Confirm verifier is defined and is explicitly forbidden from writing files
Confirm AGENTS.md section 3 names the same six agents with matching responsibilities

description: Research round 2 completes and resolves the blocking gaps G1-G4 and the payout question, with every claim citing a raw source capture.
steps: Open research/reports/ and confirm a report exists for each of the eight tracks R1-R8
Open docs/wiki/20-affiliate-programs/ALIEXPRESS-AFFILIATE.md and confirm gaps G1-G4 are marked resolved with the specific evidence that resolved them
Confirm the signing algorithm question (MD5/HMAC vs HMAC-SHA256) has one documented, cited answer
Confirm the payout question has a documented answer for a Russian ИП, and that the source is primary
Confirm every claim marked HARD FACT links to a file under research/raw/

description: A Russian/CIS competitive analysis exists, closing gap G16 — the current competitive analysis is skewed toward Western tools.
steps: Open docs/wiki/60-product-synthesis/COMPETITIVE-LANDSCAPE.md and confirm gap G16 is marked resolved
Confirm the page names at least three Russian-language price trackers or deal aggregators
For each named RU competitor, confirm a raw source capture exists under research/raw/r07-product-synthesis/
Confirm a positioning statement exists that distinguishes this project from the RU competitors specifically

description: SPEC-001-ingestion-engine.md is approved: defines the module plugin contract, idempotent upserts, watermark-based incremental sync, exponential backoff with jitter, dead-letter handling, and a request budget that respects the API's daily quota.
steps: Open docs/specs/SPEC-001-ingestion-engine.md and confirm all nine mandatory SDD sections are present
Confirm the Out of Scope section explicitly excludes anything not named in the spec
Confirm FR requirements are numbered and use RFC 2119 keywords
Confirm every AC references at least one FR or NFR
Confirm a data-retention policy is specified per field class, because affiliate API terms may forbid long retention
Confirm the spec's status field reads 'Approved'

description: SPEC-003-schema.md is approved: a Postgres-compatible schema with SQLite working locally, including explicit retention policy columns and a price-history table sized against real request-volume assumptions.
steps: Open docs/specs/SPEC-003-schema.md and confirm all nine SDD sections are present
Confirm the schema uses no Postgres-only feature that breaks under SQLite, or that the deviation is documented
Confirm the sizing section shows rows/day, GB/year and index cost arithmetic rather than asserting a conclusion
Confirm price-history retention and downsampling rules are specified
Confirm migration files exist under db/migrations/ and apply cleanly in both a fresh SQLite database and a fresh Postgres database

description: SPEC-004-static-first-web.md is approved: every page ships as static server-rendered HTML, every page has an .md twin, llms.txt is generated at build time, and Link headers advertise the markdown versions.
steps: Open docs/specs/SPEC-004-static-first-web.md and confirm all nine SDD sections are present
Confirm the spec states that no page content may depend on client-side JavaScript
Confirm the spec defines the .md URL convention (extension replaced or appended, consistently)
Confirm the spec defines the robots.txt policy for OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot, and at least two other named AI crawlers
Confirm a test strategy exists that fails the build if any page's content is absent from the server-rendered HTML

description: ADR-001 through ADR-004 are written, covering static-first framework choice, hosting, ORM choice, and markdown-serving mechanism.
steps: List docs/adr/ — at least four ADR files exist
Each ADR states Context, the decision, at least two alternatives considered with pros and cons, and consequences
ADR-001 compares Next.js and Astro explicitly, since the operator named both
ADR-002 states whether Cloudflare Pages accepts payment from a Russian ИП and whether Workers can reach the affiliate API, marking unverified items as UNVERIFIED

description: A SQLite database can be created from migrations on a fresh checkout with a single documented command, containing the full product schema.
steps: Clone or open the repo fresh and run the documented setup command
The command completes without error and prints the database path
Open the database and confirm the expected tables exist, including a product table and a price-history table
Run the migrations a second time and confirm they are idempotent — no error, no data loss
evidence: 11/11 checks passed. Migrations apply in 79 ms (NFR-4 target <10 s). Re-run applies 0 and loses 0 rows. 24 tables, all 23 required by SPEC-003 section 6 present. All 11 money columns INTEGER, 0 float (FR-3). Drift detection refuses an edit to an applied migration. 0 FK violations. 42/42 tests, typecheck clean.
known_gaps: SPEC-003 AC-2 (same migrations on Postgres) is INCONCLUSIVE - no Postgres server on this machine (no Docker, no psql). Recorded in ADR-003. This is NOT a passing test.

description: A CSV feed of products can be ingested into the database end to end, with no affiliate API credentials required.
steps: Place a small CSV fixture with at least 50 realistic product rows under the test fixtures directory
Run the documented ingest command against the fixture
The command exits zero and prints a count of rows ingested
Query the database and confirm the product count matches the fixture row count
Run the same ingest command a second time and confirm the product count is unchanged (idempotent upsert)
Modify one field in the fixture, re-run, and confirm only that row changed
evidence: 15/15 checks passed. 66 fixture rows read; 56 stored + 10 safety-excluded = 66 (none lost). Re-run: products 56->56, observations 56->56, exclusions 10->10, reports 0 written / 56 unchanged. Changing one field updates exactly 1 product row and adds NO price point. Unknown shipping stored as NULL with is_complete=0, never 0. All money columns still INTEGER after ingest. Every product traceable to a run. 102/102 tests, typecheck clean.
known_gaps: Uses a CSV fixture, not the live AliExpress API (blocked on credentials, issue #1). Temu is not ingested: no public API exists.

description: Price history is recorded over time, so that a product queried after multiple ingests returns more than one historical price point.
steps: Ingest the fixture, then change the price in the fixture and ingest again
Query price history for one product_id and confirm two or more rows exist with distinct timestamps
Confirm each row records the source of the observation (csv, api, manual)
Confirm the retention/downsampling rule from SPEC-003 is applied and documented in the output
evidence: 10/10 checks passed. Product 33006951783: 2026-10-01=18.50 -> 2026-10-05=14.99, two distinct historical points with source recorded. A price-only change reports rowsWritten 1; a no-op re-ingest reports 0. Re-ingesting an unchanged feed on 3 later dates adds 0 duplicate points. The daily rollup survives deletion of all raw observations (FR-18), and retention_policy has the correct rollup target. 113/113 tests, typecheck clean.
known_gaps: The retention job itself (FR-16/FR-17) is not implemented - only the configuration and the rollup target are. Retention defaults are conservative and NOT ToS-sourced (gap M6).

description: A product can be looked up by free-text query and by category filter through a typed API, using Postgres full-text search.
steps: Start the API using the documented command
Send a GET request for a search term that matches fixture data and confirm a JSON array of matching products
Send the same request with a category filter and confirm only that category's products are returned
Send a request for a term matching nothing and confirm an empty array with HTTP 200, not an error
Send a request with a malformed query parameter and confirm a clear 400 with a descriptive message
evidence: VERIFIED 18/18 over real HTTP: API started as a child process on a real port and queried with fetch. Free-text, category, destination filters return correct rows; no-match returns [] with HTTP 200; malformed limit returns 400 with a descriptive message. Postgres FTS remains an INCONCLUSIVE gap (no server on this machine) — the local path is case-insensitive LIKE.

description: The AliExpress module authenticates against the real affiliate API and makes one budgeted, successful product query.
steps: Place the app key and app secret in a .env file that is gitignored
Confirm `git status --porcelain` does not list .env
Run the documented smoke-test command
The command authenticates successfully and returns at least one real product
Run the command twice and confirm the request counter increases by exactly the expected number of calls

description: Affiliate deep links are generated correctly for an ingested product, and the link encodes the operator's tracking identifier.
steps: Take a product_id present in the database and call the link-generation endpoint
Confirm the returned URL points to the expected AliExpress product page
Confirm the URL contains the operator's affiliate tracking identifier in the correct parameter
Confirm the generated link for a product with no commission yields a clearly-marked non-monetised result rather than a broken link
Confirm the endpoint enforces the per-programme geo policy and refuses to generate a link for a prohibited region

description: Safety-critical product categories are excluded from the database and from all generated content.
steps: Load a fixture containing products from batteries, chargers, PPE and baby-goods categories alongside normal products
Run ingestion and confirm the safety-critical rows are rejected with a logged reason
Confirm they are absent from the lookup API results
Confirm the rejection is logged to the audit log with the category that caused it
Confirm the exclusion list is configurable and documented, not hardcoded in the query
evidence: VERIFIED as part of F014/F017 (18/18). 11 safety-critical fixture rows excluded at ingest with matched category+keyword, absent from catalogue AND from the API; 66-11=55 reconciles. Configurable via SAFETY_EXCLUDED_CATEGORIES, documented in .env.example, no keyword literals in schema DDL. Found and fixed a real under-exclusion: Wireless Charging Pad passed while Wireless Charger Stand was excluded (D-031).

description: A single product page renders as static HTML containing the product title, price, and an affiliate link, with no content dependent on JavaScript.
steps: Build the site and serve it locally
Fetch the product page HTML with JavaScript disabled, or inspect the raw HTML response
Confirm the product title and price are present in the raw HTML source
Confirm the affiliate link is present in the raw HTML source
Confirm an .md twin of the same page is fetchable and contains the same factual content

description: The site publishes a valid llms.txt, a sitemap.xml, and a robots.txt that explicitly permits AI search crawlers.
steps: Fetch /llms.txt and confirm it parses as Markdown with an H1, a blockquote summary, and H2 sections of links
Confirm every link in llms.txt resolves to a page that actually exists
Fetch /robots.txt and confirm OAI-SearchBot is allowed
Confirm the site returns a Link header with rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" pointing at a .md twin
Confirm /sitemap.xml exists and lists the product pages

description: An automated test fails the build if any page's primary content is absent from the server-rendered HTML, guarding the HTML-first requirement permanently.
steps: Run the full test suite and confirm it passes
Temporarily replace a page's server-rendered content with client-only rendering
Re-run the suite and confirm the guard test FAILS with a message naming the offending page
Restore the page and confirm the suite passes again

description: A landed-cost page shows item price, shipping and any known duty/VAT, and explicitly states what it does not include.
steps: Open a product page for an item with known shipping cost
Confirm the page shows item price, shipping, and a computed total
Confirm the page states in visible text which cost components are not included
Open a product page for an item where shipping is unknown and confirm the page says so rather than showing zero
Confirm no page ever presents an incomplete total as if it were complete

description: A Telegram bot delivers price-drop alerts for products a user has subscribed to.
steps: Start the bot with a valid bot token supplied via environment variable
Send the bot a subscribe command for a product that exists in the database
Change that product's price in the database and run a price-change check
Confirm the bot sends a message within one minute containing the old price, the new price and a working affiliate link
Confirm the message includes a clear affiliate-disclosure line

description: Traffic to the site is measured per channel, so that EPC and clicks-per-channel are known.
steps: Visit the site from three distinguishable referrer channels
Confirm three distinct click events are recorded with their channel labels
Open the analytics view and confirm clicks per channel are correct
Confirm a conversion event can be recorded against a click
Confirm EPC per channel can be computed from clicks and commissions

description: CI runs the full test ladder on every pull request and blocks merges on failure.
steps: Open a pull request with a deliberately failing test
Confirm CI runs and reports the failure
Confirm the pull request cannot be merged while CI is red
Fix the test, push, and confirm CI goes green
Confirm CI runs lint, unit, contract, integration and golden-file tests

description: The site is deployed to Cloudflare and is publicly reachable, with a documented rollback procedure.
steps: Follow the documented deploy command and confirm the deployment succeeds
Open the deployed URL and confirm the product page renders correctly
Fetch the .md twin on the deployed domain and confirm it exists
Deploy a known-bad build and confirm the documented rollback command restores the previous working version
Confirm the rollback procedure is written in docs/runbooks/

description: The site is live with at least one indexed, affiliate-linked page, and an affiliate click is recorded end to end.
steps: Confirm the site is publicly reachable and a product page contains a working affiliate link
Click the affiliate link and confirm the destination is the correct product page on the marketplace
Confirm the click appears in the network's affiliate dashboard
Confirm the click is recorded by the site's own analytics
Confirm the recorded click count matches between the site and the network dashboard

description: A first real commission is received and reconciled against the platform's own records.
steps: Confirm at least one qualifying order has reached Trade Completed or equivalent status in the affiliate dashboard
Confirm the commission amount appears in a payout statement
Confirm the payout was received by the ИП bank account
Compare the platform's expected commission against the actual payout and confirm the difference is explained
Append the reconciliation result to docs/logs/DECISION_LOG.md
